provisions.title: Counted strike (legal strikes)
provisions.body:
During the fights of each category, the number of strikes by the blade of the weapon delivered into the legal strike zone of the opponent’s body is counted.
A counted strike is considered a strike if it was clear and deliberate, and the opponent failed to counter it effectively with a defensive action.

provisions.title: Prohibited Strike Zones (illegal strikes)
provisions.body: The following zones are “illegal strikes” and will not count for your score. Striking into these zones can result in penalties or disqualification.

provisions.title: Back and Front of the Neck
provisions.body: Strikes to the back and front of the neck are prohibited.

provisions.title: Base of Skull
provisions.body: The base of the skull is considered a prohibited strike zone, specifically defined as the bottom third of the back of the helmet.

provisions.title: Back of Knee
provisions.body: Strikes to the back of the knee are prohibited. No pressure is to be placed on the back of the knee.

provisions.title: Groin and Crotch
provisions.body: Strikes to the groin and crotch are prohibited.

provisions.title: Feet and Ankles
provisions.body: Strikes to the feet and ankles are prohibited. However, striking the foot is not considered a prohibited strike if the competitor raises their foot while the strike is already occurring.

provisions.title: Unprotected Body Parts
provisions.body: Any part of the opponent’s body that has lost itself protection is considered a prohibited strike zone.

provisions.title: Sword and Shield
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal striking zone of the opponent will score:
● 2 points:
○ Head ○ Torso
● 1 point:
○ Legs ○ Arms ○ Hands

provisions.title: Sword and Buckler
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal striking zone of the opponent will score:
● 1 point

provisions.title: Polearm
provisions.body:
The full length of the cutting edge of the weapon is considered a blade.
Offensive actions with the haft of the polearm do not score.
The grip must be held with 2 hands for a strike to be counted.

Each strike to the legal striking zone of the opponent will score:
● 0 point:
○ Hands
● 1 point:
○ All other legal striking zones

provisions.title: Longsword
provisions.body:
Each strike to the legal striking zone of the opponent will score:
2 hands holding the grip:
● 2 points:
○ Head ○ Torso
● 1 point:
○ Arms ○ Legs ○ Hands 1 hand holding the grip:
● 1 point:
○ All legal striking zones

provisions.title: Sword and Buckler
provisions.body:
A match is won by the first competitor who has 2 round victories.
A round is won by the competitor who has either:
● scored 5 points first before the time limit, or
● scored more points than their opponent if the time limit has been reached.
The maximum score for a round is 5 points.
The maximum time limit for a round is 1 minute.
There is no break in between rounds.

provisions.title: Polearm, Longsword and Sword and Shield
provisions.body:
A match is won by the competitor who has scored at least 2 more points than their opponent during the overall match.
The score of the match is the sum of the scores of the rounds.
A match consists of 2 main rounds of 1 minute each.
If the score difference between the 2 competitors is less than 2 points after the 2 main rounds, additional 30-second rounds are fought until the 2-point difference is reached.
There is a 30-second break in between rounds.

Important!
The organizers can change the length of the round, provided this decision is coordinated with the Head Organization and is registered in the Tournament Regulations.

provisions.title: Technical win
provisions.body: A “technical win” is awarded to one of the competitors in the following cases:

provisions.title: Withdrawal
provisions.body:
A competitor is considered as withdrawn is they either:
● Failed to report to the list upon the Head Referee’s call.
● Failed to prepare the equipment within the designated time.
● Withdraws before the match has started.
The competitor who failed to report to the list for the match may be penalized by a yellow card.
In the case a competitor cannot participate in the competition because of an injury or disqualification, their opponent is awarded a technical win.

provisions.title: Injury
provisions.body:
If the competitor cannot continue the match due to the injury caused by an illegal strike, their opponent receives a penalty of a red card and is banned from further participation in the tournament.
The severity of the injury must be assessed by the designated medics of the tournament.
The injured competitor is awarded a technical win.
The injured competitor is withdrawn from further matches in this category.

provisions.title: Disqualification of the opponent
provisions.body: If a competitor gets 2 yellow cards or 1 red card, all their following opponents are awarded a technical win.

provisions.title: Armor failure
provisions.body:
If the match is impeded due to equipment failure that is impossible to fix within the designated time frame of 1 minute.

Scoring for “technical win” 5-0 for 2 rounds for Sword and Buckler category 10-0 per round for all other categories

provisions.title: Authorized Fighting Techniques
provisions.body:
These rules aim to define a set of permitted and prohibited actions to ensure the safety of participants while engaging in combat.

The guidelines cover striking, grabbing, and various techniques to maintain a fair and controlled environment during the event.

provisions.title: Permitted Strikes
provisions.body:
Strikes with the blade and the haft of the weapon are permitted.
Buckler: Strikes with the flat of the buckler are permitted.
Polearm: Strikes with a free hand, if they have a weapon in the other hand, are permitted.

provisions.title: Strike Zones
provisions.body: Strikes to any area not mentioned as a prohibited strike zone are permitted.

provisions.title: Parry
provisions.body: Parrying the opponent’s strikes is permitted.

provisions.title: Techniques and moves with shields (Buckler, Sword and Shield)
provisions.body:
Pushing the opponent with the shoulder or the flat of the shield is permitted.
Pushing the blade, shield, armed hand or upper body (above the waistline) of the opponent with the flat or edge of the shield is permitted.
Using the shield to hook or cover the opponent’s shield is permitted.

provisions.title: Techniques and moves (Longsword, Polearm)
provisions.body:
Pushing the opponent with the blade or arms is permitted.
Pushing off the opponent's arms with the arms is permitted.

provisions.title: Weapon-Grabbing
provisions.body: Participants are allowed to grab their own weapon (except the blade) with their hands.

provisions.title: Pinned to the List Rail
provisions.body: Pinning an opponent to the list is not against the rules; however, if a competitor is pinned against the list rail, the Knight Marshal will call 'Break Fight' and reset the competitors to the center of the list.

provisions.title: Prohibited Fighting Techniques
provisions.body: These rules aim to ensure the safety, fairness, and adherence to a set of standards.

provisions.title: Unlisted Techniques
provisions.body: Any actions not listed in section 3 (Authorized Fighting Techniques) of the rules are prohibited.

provisions.title: Thrusting Actions
provisions.body:
Any thrusting action with a weapon is prohibited.
Threats of a thrusting action are prohibited.

provisions.title: Offensive Actions on Prohibited Strike Zones
provisions.body: Any offensive action landing on any prohibited strike zone is prohibited.

provisions.title: Striking to Grounded or Rising Competitors
provisions.body: Striking a grounded or rising competitor is prohibited.

provisions.title: Strikes to Disarmed Opponent
provisions.body: Strikes to an opponent who has lost their weapon are prohibited.

provisions.title: Strikes with the Head
provisions.body: Strikes to an opponent with the head are prohibited.

provisions.title: Strikes with Legs
provisions.body: Strikes with feet, shin, and knees are prohibited.

provisions.title: Techniques and Moves
provisions.body: Back heels, wrestling throws, and clinching are prohibited.

provisions.title: Strikes with Hands and Elbows
provisions.body:
Strikes with hands and elbows are prohibited, with the exception of the Polearm category.
See “3.1. Permitted Strikes” for details.

provisions.title: Strikes with the pommel or cross guard of a Bladed Weapon
provisions.body: Strikes delivered with the pommel or cross guard of a bladed weapon are prohibited.

provisions.title: Grappling
provisions.body:
Grappling with hands and arms to the opponent’s torso, head, and limbs.
Handholds of the opponent’s sword.
Trap opponents' weapons by shield, buckler and/or arm/hands.

provisions.title: Strikes with a Shield
provisions.body: Strikes delivered with the edge of a shield are prohibited.

provisions.title: Strikes with a Buckler
provisions.body: Strikes with the edge of a buckler are prohibited.

provisions.title: Authorized Equipment
provisions.body:
These rules aim to ensure a high standard of authenticity, safety, and historical accuracy in the equipment and conduct of the participants.

Reference all Authenticity Committee documents for the detailed rules.

provisions.title: Technical and Authentic Compliance
provisions.body:
All equipment must meet Buhurt International technical and authentic requirements.
Reference:
● “Armors and Weapons Aesthetics and Decorations” document for the rules.
● ”Technical Requirements for Weapons” document.
● ”Technical Requirements for Armors” document.

provisions.title: Competitor Eligibility
provisions.body: Competitors are not allowed unless they have passed technical and authenticity checks.

provisions.title: Weapon Requirements
provisions.body:
Reference ”Technical Requirements for Weapons” document for all the rules.
Reference “Weapons/Shield Chart” document for sizes and weights.
Reminder: Low-quality, dirty, rusty, or historically implausible weapons are not allowed.

provisions.title: Footwear
provisions.body:
Reference ”Textiles and Leather” document for details.
Reminder: Only medieval Shoes with low profile (non-lugged/studded/spiked) are allowed.

provisions.title: Materials
provisions.body:
Reference ”Textiles and Leather” document for details.
Reminder: Modern adhesive tape, plastic ties, and other visible modern materials are not permitted.
Textile adhesive tape of neutral colors for kit repair is an exception.

provisions.title: Decorations
provisions.body:
Reference “Armors and Weapons Aesthetics and Decorations” for details.
Reminder: Slogans and imagery on equipment should be historically plausible and not derogatory.
No modern equipment or decorations are allowed.

provisions.title: Equipment Changes
provisions.body:
Participants are allowed to change elements of equipment (armor or weapon) during intervals or due to breakage.
Technical Marshal supervision is required for equipment changes.

provisions.title: Management of the competitors
provisions.body: Management of the competitors is conducted in accordance with the Buhurt International Duels Regulations, with penalties that are imposed depending on the situation in the list and competitors’ and marshals’ actions.

provisions.title: Changelog
provisions.body:
This will be the change log of this document. It will be updated regularly and will display what has been removed/added/reworded/formatted. This way BI keeps transparent communication and clarity about the rules.

April - 2026 (V. 26.4) Formatting redone for consistency and readability. Except points listed below, no content changes.
Grammatical corrections were also made.
Clarification:
- Titles for 1.3.1. “Cases For Grounding” and 1.3.2. “Cases for Not Grounding”. No content changes except:
- “While not carrying a weapon in your hand you're not allowed to engage in offensive actions [...]” to “While not carrying a weapon in their hand, they engaged in offensive actions [...]”
- “Any part of a polearm, a sword blade or mace is not considered as contacting the ground.” yo “They touched the ground with any part of a weapon”.
Add:
- 3.”Authorized Equipement”: Multiple references to AC documents for details.
- 4.3. Weapon-Grabbing: “Grabbing your own blade by the hand is not allowed.”
- 4.5. Weapon Loss: “Grab a weapon left on the table top by an active fighter.” Clarification:
- 6.4.2. No “wide” top bar list
- 4. Authorized Fighting Techniques: Introduction paragraph moved to 4.5. Weapon Loss section.
Add:
- 2.3.2. Injury: “The severity of the injury must be assessed by the designated medics of the tournament.” Clarification:
- 2.3. Technical win: scores are per round
- 4.3. Offensive Actions on Prohibited Strike Zones: “Any offensive action landing on any prohibited strike zone is prohibited.”
- Split of 4.9. Punches and elbow strikes in: 4.9.Strikes with Hands and Elbows and 4.13.
Suppression:
- 5.1. General Requirements: title has been removed for uselessness. Subsequent titles have been moved up.
Add:
- 5. ”Authorized Equipement”: Multiple references to AC documents for details.

Update: January 2026 -add: 2.2.1 In case of a draw, fight additional rounds until one competitors has two round victories -add: 4.11 Trap opponents' weapons by shield, buckler and/or arm/hands.
-add: 5.1.4 Medieval Shoes with low profile (non lugged/studded/spiked) soles as referenced in Authenticity Standards.

Update: october 2025
- add: 1.2.

Update: March 2025 -add: 3.7 Pinned to the List Rail

To see older changelogs, please refer to the archived documents.
